A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CTTA survey, with complete, readable text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendix A. Content can be matched reliably despite localized edits and figure relocation.

before.justification: Section 7 explicitly sources benchmark results from prior publications and benchmark studies. Figure 2 reports annual publication counts without specifying their provenance or computation, leaving original data-analysis attribution unresolved. Appendix A contains no empirical study.

after.justification: Section 7 retains the explicit attribution of benchmark results to prior studies. Figure 2 retains publication counts with unspecified provenance, so their status as original data analysis remains unclear. Appendix A adds no empirical results.

M1.justification: The survey retains the same taxonomy and methods. Revised equations and expanded descriptions clarify existing approaches; they do not introduce a proposed algorithm or establish changes to an implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Tables 4–7 retain CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, ImageNet-C, and Cityscapes-to-ACDC coverage. Other dataset descriptions and discussed deployment scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each of Tables 4–7. Expanded explanations of LAW and normalization methods do not add or remove methods from the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 3 rewrites the sample-count description but retains 10,000 samples per CIFAR corruption domain and 5,000 for ImageNet-C. Evaluation architectures, severity, metrics, sequencing, and the segmentation comparison's ten rounds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness test, sensitivity study, or case study is added or revised. The existing long-term stability and hyperparameter sensitivity summaries in Section 7.6 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other evaluation uncertainty reporting. The benchmark tables retain the same point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 4–7 and their reported findings are unchanged, including RMT's 13.9% CIFAR-10-C error and 54.8% ImageNet-C error, and Hybrid-TTA's 62.2% segmentation mIoU. Figure 2's publication counts are also identical.

T1.justification: Equation 2 replaces an exact entropy argmin with an explicit gradient update. Section 4.2.2 revises Equation 21 to use a negative-log-likelihood gradient and clarifies the scalar diagonal-Fisher formulation. These are localized mathematical revisions; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the CTTA taxonomy, problem formulation, benchmark synthesis, and future directions. Their language edits do not change the claimed scope or contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations of benchmark findings, method failure conditions, applicability boundaries, and deployment limitations remain unchanged. The added channel-wise and scalar-gradient explanations clarify technical mechanics without changing the substantive conclusions.

D1.justification: Section 4.2.2 newly specifies that LAW averages diagonal Fisher estimates over parameters within each layer. Section 4.2.1 makes channel-wise normalization operations explicit. These document existing methods more precisely without establishing changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: The reference list and positioning relative to earlier surveys and CTTA methods are unchanged. GOLD's citation gains parentheses in Table 3, which is a formatting correction.

P1.justification: Localized language edits affect the abstract, contributions, and method descriptions, with expanded explanations of pseudo-label notation, BatchNorm, and LAW. The section hierarchy remains intact, and the first author gains an equal-contribution marker.

P2.justification: Figures 8 and 9 move from pages 22 and 23 to pages 23 and 24, respectively, while retaining their content and captions. Revised equations and text cause limited reflow; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The explicit online update in Equation 2 and clearer descriptions of channel-wise normalization and LAW's layer aggregation modestly improve technical readability while preserving the evidence and scope. The benefit is limited: the new description of Equation 22's uncentered second moment as an empirical variance introduces mathematical imprecision.
